name: Thich Nhat Hanh
tagline: The Zen master who coined "Engaged Buddhism" and taught the world the miracle of mindfulness.
journey: During the Vietnam War, he refused to take sides, instead working to rebuild bombed villages, set up schools, and advocate for peace. Exiled from his homeland for his peace activism, he established Plum Village in France and became a global spiritual leader, teaching millions how to find peace in a cup of tea or a simple footstep.
trial: His trial was maintaining absolute non-violence and deep compassion while witnessing the violent destruction of his country, proving that mindfulness is not an escape from reality, but a way to heal it.
teaching: Smile, breathe and go slowly. Peace is every step.
moral: Peace is not an external goal; it is the very path you walk upon.
journey_local: वियतनाम युद्ध के दौरान, उन्होंने शांति की वकालत की। अपनी शांति सक्रियता के लिए निर्वासित होने पर, उन्होंने फ्रांस में प्लम विलेज की स्थापना की और एक वैश्विक आध्यात्मिक नेता बने।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण अपने देश के हिंसक विनाश को देखते हुए पूर्ण अहिंसा और गहरी करुणा बनाए रखना था।
teaching_local: मुस्कुराओ, सांस लो और धीरे चलो। शांति हर कदम में है।
moral_local: शांति कोई बाहरी लक्ष्य नहीं है; यह वह मार्ग है जिस पर आप चलते हैं।

name: Sant Tukaram
tagline: The grocer-saint whose Abhangs became the heartbeat of Maharashtra's Varkari tradition.
journey: Bankrupt and having lost his family to famine, Tukaram turned entirely to Lord Vithoba. He composed thousands of passionate Marathi poems (Abhangs) that broke down the complex Vedas into simple devotional songs accessible to the common masses.
trial: Orthodox Brahmins threw his manuscript of poems into the river. He fasted on the riverbank until the river miraculously returned the intact manuscript.
teaching: Words are the only jewels I possess, words are the only clothes I wear, words are the only food that sustains my life.
moral: Sincere devotion in your mother tongue is as sacred as the oldest Sanskrit chant.
journey_local: दिवालिया होने और अकाल में अपने परिवार को खोने के बाद, तुकाराम पूरी तरह से भगवान विठोबा की ओर मुड़ गए।
trial_local: रूढ़िवादियों ने उनकी कविताओं की पांडुलिपि नदी में फेंक दी। नदी ने चमत्कारिक रूप से अक्षुण्ण पांडुलिपि लौटा दी।
teaching_local: शब्द ही मेरे पास एकमात्र गहने हैं, शब्द ही मेरा जीवन हैं।
moral_local: आपकी मातृभाषा में सच्ची भक्ति सबसे पुराने संस्कृत मंत्र के समान पवित्र है।

name: Goswami Tulsidas
tagline: The passionate lover whose heartbreak turned into the Ramcharitmanas, the Bible of North India.
journey: Obsessively in love with his wife Ratnavali, he crossed a flooded river holding a corpse, mistaking it for a log, just to see her. She rebuked him: "If you had half as much love for Rama as you have for this flesh, you would cross the ocean of existence." Instantly awakened, he renounced the world and wrote the epic Ramcharitmanas in the local Awadhi language.
trial: He faced massive persecution from Sanskrit scholars in Varanasi for daring to write scripture in the language of the common people.
teaching: Siya Ram may sab jag jaani, karahu pranaam jori jug paani.
moral: Worldly heartbreak is often the catalyst for divine awakening.
journey_local: अपनी पत्नी की फटकार के बाद, उन्होंने संसार का त्याग कर दिया और स्थानीय अवधी भाषा में महाकाव्य रामचरितमानस लिखा।
trial_local: आम लोगों की भाषा में शास्त्र लिखने की हिम्मत करने के लिए उन्हें वाराणसी में संस्कृत विद्वानों से भारी उत्पीड़न का सामना करना पड़ा।
teaching_local: सिया राम मय सब जग जानी, करहुं प्रणाम जोरि जुग पानी।
moral_local: सांसारिक दिल टूटना अक्सर ईश्वरीय जागृति का उत्प्रेरक होता है।

name: Maharishi Valmiki
tagline: The highway robber who transformed into the First Poet (Adi Kavi) and authored the Ramayana.
journey: Born as Ratnakar, a violent bandit who supported his family through robbery. Sage Narada made him realize that his family would share his wealth, but not his karma. Horrified, he sat in meditation chanting "Mara Mara" (which became "Rama Rama") for so long that an anthill (Valmika) formed over him.
trial: His trial was completely shedding his violent past and purifying his consciousness to such an extent that he became the pure vessel for the world's first epic poetry.
teaching: Even the worst sinner can attain the highest spiritual state through honest repentance and chanting the Divine Name.
moral: Your past does not dictate your spiritual future.
journey_local: रत्नाकर के रूप में जन्मे, एक हिंसक डाकू जो डकैती के माध्यम से अपने परिवार का भरण-पोषण करता था। उन्होंने ध्यान किया और वाल्मीकि बने।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण अपने हिंसक अतीत को पूरी तरह से छोड़ना और अपनी चेतना को शुद्ध करना था।
teaching_local: ईमानदार पश्चाताप और भगवान के नाम का जाप करके सबसे बड़ा पापी भी उच्चतम आध्यात्मिक स्थिति प्राप्त कर सकता है।
moral_local: आपका अतीत आपके आध्यात्मिक भविष्य को निर्धारित नहीं करता है।

name: Vyasa
tagline: Compiler of the Mahabharata, a foundational sage of ancient India.
journey: Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa is identified as the author of the Mahabharata. The sources consistently present him as the central figure who compiled and structured this great epic. His name itself, Krishna-Dwaipayana, points to his origins. The texts are attributed directly to him, establishing his role as the foundational compiler of this vast narrative.
trial: The sources do not describe a specific personal trial or spiritual crisis for Vyasa. His life is presented through his monumental work. The defining aspect of his existence, as per the sources, is the immense task of compiling the Mahabharata, which serves as his primary narrative and contribution.
teaching: Vyasa's core teaching is embodied in the Mahabharata, a text he compiled. This epic serves as a comprehensive guide to dharma, exploring complex moral and ethical dilemmas through its narratives. His contribution is the preservation and structuring of this vast knowledge for future generations, making it accessible.
moral: A modern seeker can learn from Vyasa's dedication to preserving and organizing profound wisdom. His life exemplifies the importance of making complex knowledge accessible and structured for the benefit of society. The moral is in the act of compilation and transmission of essential teachings.
legacy: Vyasa's legacy is the Mahabharata itself, a foundational text of Indian culture and spirituality. By compiling this epic, he shaped the tradition and lineage of dharma for millennia. His work has become a primary source of moral and philosophical guidance in the Hindu tradition.
journey_local: कृष्णद्वैपायन व्यास महाभारतका संकलक हुन्।
trial_local: व्यासको जीवनमा कुनै विशिष्ट व्यक्तिगत परीक्षण वा आध्यात्मिक सङ्कटको वर्णन गरिएको छैन।
teaching_local: व्यासको मुख्य योगदान महाभारतको संकलन हो, जसले धर्मको विस्तृत मार्गदर्शकको रूपमा काम गर्दछ।
moral_local: आधुनिक साधक व्यासको गहन ज्ञानको संरक्षण र सङ्गठनप्रतिको समर्पणबाट सिक्न सक्छन्।
legacy_local: व्यासको विरासत महाभारत हो, जुन भारतीय संस्कृति र आध्यात्मिकताको आधारभूत ग्रन्थ हो।

name: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)
tagline: The intrepid pilgrim who crossed deserts and mountains to bring pure Buddhist scriptures from India to China.
journey: Disturbed by conflicting translations of Buddhist texts in China, Xuanzang defied an imperial travel ban to journey to the source: India. He crossed the deadly Taklamakan Desert and the towering Hindu Kush. He studied at Nalanda University under Silabhadra, mastered Sanskrit, and collected hundreds of texts. He then journeyed back and spent the rest of his life translating them, fundamentally shaping East Asian Buddhism.
trial: He faced freezing mountains, bandits, and near-starvation in the desert, driven solely by a singular, burning desire for uncorrupted truth.
teaching: I would rather die heading West [to India] than live by returning to the East.
moral: The pursuit of truth is worth any distance, any danger, and any sacrifice.
journey_local: चीन में बौद्ध ग्रंथों के परस्पर विरोधी अनुवादों से परेशान होकर, ह्वेन त्सांग ने स्रोत: भारत की यात्रा करने के लिए एक शाही यात्रा प्रतिबंध को धता बता दी। उन्होंने नालंदा विश्वविद्यालय में अध्ययन किया और संस्कृत में महारत हासिल की।
trial_local: उन्होंने बर्फीले पहाड़ों, डाकुओं और रेगिस्तान में लगभग भुखमरी का सामना किया, जो पूरी तरह से असंबद्ध सत्य की एक विलक्षण, ज्वलंत इच्छा से प्रेरित था।
teaching_local: मैं पूर्व में लौटने के बजाय पश्चिम [भारत] की ओर जाते हुए मरना पसंद करूँगा।
moral_local: सत्य की खोज किसी भी दूरी, किसी भी खतरे और किसी भी बलिदान के लायक है।

name: Yashovijaya
tagline: The intellectual giant who went to Varanasi in disguise to master and harmonize Indian logic.
journey: A Jain monk who desired to study the advanced Nyaya (logic) systems available only to Brahmins in Varanasi. He lived there in disguise, mastering the texts. When his identity was discovered, rather than being punished, his teachers were astonished by his brilliance. He returned and wrote over 100 texts in Sanskrit and Gujarati, revitalizing Jain logic.
trial: His trial was dedicating his life to rigorous, dry logic, yet keeping his heart moist with deep devotion and humility, proving that sharp intellect and deep spirituality can coexist.
teaching: Logic without devotion is barren; devotion without logic is blind.
moral: Pursue knowledge fiercely, but never let it inflate your ego.
journey_local: एक जैन भिक्षु जो उन्नत न्याय प्रणालियों का अध्ययन करना चाहता था। वह भेष बदलकर वाराणसी में रहे और ग्रंथों में महारत हासिल की।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण अपने जीवन को कठोर तर्क के लिए समर्पित करना था, फिर भी अपने दिल को गहरी भक्ति और विनम्रता से नम रखना था।
teaching_local: भक्ति के बिना तर्क बंजर है; तर्क के बिना भक्ति अंधी है।
moral_local: ज्ञान का दृढ़ता से पीछा करें, लेकिन इसे कभी भी अपने अहंकार को बढ़ाने न दें।
